title: Two bonded layers in one curved strip
before: The object comprises a clamp, an outer layer and a support layer. The two layers have a curved shape. They have the same width. The outside layer is thin, and the inside layer is thicker. Both are continuous and bonded along the full length. One end of both layers is held by the clamp. The other end is free. The view of the end repeats this end of the same object. This is a fictional structural schematic, not a test of bending or adhesion.
after: A single curved strip consists of two continuous layers of equal width: a thin layer along the outer side of the curve and a thicker support layer along the inner side. The layers are bonded over their full length, with no separation, and extend to a common free end; their opposite ends are held together in an opaque clamp. The enlarged view repeats the free end of this same strip. This fictional schematic describes a static structure only; it does not specify how the curvature was formed or represent a bending or adhesion test.
caption: Fictional two-layer curved strip. The thin outer layer and thicker inner support share the same width and remain bonded throughout, from the opaque clamp to the common free end. The dashed outline and link identify an enlarged view of that same terminal face, not a second strip. Colours distinguish the two materials; shading indicates surface orientation. Geometry and layer thicknesses are schematic and not to scale. No loading, motion or material response is depicted.
